item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.15：Game Mode，给拇指一个掌机
item.content:encoded:
两只拇指已经占满了​

你双手捧着手机，游戏却同时要你做三件事：向左，开火，跳。

屏幕键盘拿来敲 MOUNT C . 很顺手，拿来玩游戏就很别扭。一只拇指按在方向键上，另一只得离开方向键去够字母 B——就那么一两秒，而带计时的游戏不会给你这一两秒。

于是你只挑那些单手能玩的游戏，或者干脆不玩。

1.0.0.15 给键盘添了第二张脸。

屏幕键盘上的这些控制台风格按键。Game Mode 要替换的就是它们——这张图拍的是按键，不是手柄。

按键翻成手柄​

Game Mode 就住在键盘面板里。键盘显示着的时候，打开 Caps Lock（不想找它的话，双击 Shift 就行），然后敲一段人人都已经存在手指里的暗号：

  ↑  ↑  ↓  ↓  ←  →  ←  →  B  A

按键翻面了。原来的 QWERTY 变成一个八向方向键、一个轨迹球，外加 DOS 游戏真正用来开火、跳跃和横移的那几个键：Y、X、CTRL、ALT、SPACE 和 ENT。

方向键是你用得最多的，也是你会按得最狠的：八个方向，一根拇指，不用够。

必须大写的两个字母​

这段暗号是按字母实际打出来的大小写来匹配的。

听着像是吹毛求疵，其实不是：你打一个小写的 "ba"，模拟器就老老实实照做——把 "ba" 打进了 DOS 提示符。你就坐在 C:\> 面前，屏幕上多了两个莫名其妙的字母，游戏根本没开始。

所以 B 和 A 必须是大写。Caps Lock 不是建议。

要退回去，在方向键上敲同一段暗号，然后按 X、Y。或者按手机的返回键——它退出 Game Mode 和退出键盘一样干脆。

屏幕更窄时的按键布局——每一颗键都得挤出自己的位置。

每个键都能重新映射​

每个游戏都想把按钮放在自己顺手的地方。有的游戏用 X 开火，有的用 Y，都很常见，而且多半都不合你的手。

长按那个金色的档案按钮，选 Remap buttons…。在手柄上按一个键，再按你更想要的那个键，替换就成了。

这套映射属于这一个游戏，并且会被记住。同一个游戏下次打开还是老样子——配一次，就一直在。

这个手柄就是键盘​

下面这件事是看不见的，也是我自己最满意的部分。

手柄发出的 SDL 事件，和屏幕键盘发出的完全一样。运行在 DOS 里的程序分辨不出两者的差别。没有一条新的输入通路需要游戏去学，没有新的驱动，1994 年的游戏也不需要因此多一份疑心。手柄上的一个按钮就是一个按键，跟键盘上的一个键没有区别。

轨迹球也是同一个道理：它发出的是相对位移的鼠标事件，和真实鼠标发的那种一样，SDL 这一层现在接受它们了。

整个设计就是这样：键盘长出了第二层皮，而不是变成了另一台机器。

模拟器里跑着的游戏，两侧是键盘的按键——正是那种会想要一只手柄的游戏。

退出应用不再崩​

同一版里还带了一个小修复。

以前关机的过程中一旦出错，进程会被 SIGABRT 直接打死——偏偏是在它自己正准备退出的那一刻崩掉，这个时机很怪。现在这个错误会被接住，退出流程照常走完。

这件事我不会写进标题。但一个退出时都会死掉的模拟器，会让人开始不信任它；我更希望它只是安安静静地走掉。

存档还是读得出来​

存档格式什么都没改。 Game Mode 只是换了一种按同样的键的方式，所以之前各版本写下的存档都照常读得出来。

这一条比功能本身还重要。一次悄悄改掉格式的发布，会留下一批再也打不开的存档；老实做法是——格式真变了就大声改，带版本号地改。

文档也跟上了​

用户手册多了一章讲手柄，技术参考多出了手柄那一节和真实的按键路径，中断表里多了一个案例：一个手指如何变成一个 DOS 按键。

文档里所有用字符画出来的方框图也都换成了 SVG，边框笔直，所以无论在哪个渲染器、哪种字体里，都还是那个方框。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装上一版：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.15

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.15.apk
size:   16 500 506 bytes
sha256: dbf776abe6b69541194fa5bded5d2c807a94add4733a74ea2620b03227263f42

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身，那里的 Game Mode 章节才是真正的说明——包括你重新映射之后各个键到底做什么。请去读那份，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄壳，Game Mode 不过是那层壳上的另一层。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担——现在手柄也归它管，毕竟一路到底都是同一批事件。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

一根拇指可以同时按住一个方向、一个键和一颗球。而那款写于 1994 年的游戏，永远不需要知道这中间的差别。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.15: Game Mode, a console-style gamepad for your thumb
item.content:encoded:
Your thumbs are already full​

You are holding the phone in two hands and the game wants three things at once: go left, fire, jump.

The on-screen keyboard is a good way to type MOUNT C . and a bad way to play that. One thumb sits on the arrow pads, the other thumb has to leave them to find the letter B, and for a second — a second that a game with a timer does not give you — nobody is steering.

So you choose a game you can play with one thumb, or you do not choose it at all.

1.0.0.15 gives the keyboard a second face.

The console-style pads of the on-screen keyboard. This is the layout Game Mode replaces — the picture shows the pads, not the gamepad.

The pads turn into a gamepad​

Game Mode lives inside the keyboard panel. With the keyboard pads showing, switch Caps Lock on — double-tap Shift if you would rather not hunt for it — and type the code everyone already has in their fingers:

  ↑  ↑  ↓  ↓  ←  →  ←  →  B  A

The pads flip. What was a QWERTY board becomes an eight-way D-pad, a trackball, and the buttons a DOS game actually fires, jumps and strafes with: Y, X, CTRL, ALT, SPACE and ENT.

The direction pad is the one you will use most, and it is the one you will press hardest: eight directions, one thumb, no reaching.

The two letters that have to be capital​

The code is matched on the case the letters are actually typed in.

That sounds like pedantry, and it is not: type a lowercase "ba" and the emulator does exactly what you asked. It types "ba" into the DOS prompt, and you sit there at C:\> with two stray letters and a game that never started.

So the B and the A must be capital. Caps Lock is not a suggestion.

To go back, type the same code on the D-pad and then X, Y. Or press the phone's Back button, which leaves Game Mode as readily as it leaves the keyboard.

The pads on a narrower screen, where every key has to earn its room.

Every button can be remapped​

Every game wants its buttons somewhere else. The one that shoots on X and the one that shoots on Y are both common, and both are wrong for you at least once.

Long-press the gold profile button and pick Remap buttons…. Press a button on the gamepad, press the key you would rather have, and the swap is done.

The remap belongs to that one game and is remembered. The same title always plays the same way, next time and the next — you set it once and it stays.

The gamepad is a keyboard​

Here is the part I am happiest about, and it is not a feature you can see.

The gamepad sends the same SDL events the on-screen keyboard sends. The guest cannot tell the two apart. There is no new input path to teach a game, no new driver, no second set of keys for a 1994 title to be suspicious of. A button on the gamepad is a keystroke, exactly as a key on the keyboard is a keystroke.

The trackball works the same way: it sends the relative mouse events, the kind a real mouse sends, and the SDL layer now accepts them.

That is the whole design. The keyboard grew a second skin instead of becoming a new machine.

A game running in the emulator, with the keyboard's pads at the sides — the kind of game that asks for a gamepad.

Leaving the app is clean​

A smaller fix, in the same release.

A shutdown that failed used to abort the process with SIGABRT — and it did that while it was only shutting down, which is a strange time to crash. The error is caught now and the exit carries on.

I would not put this in a headline. But an emulator that dies on the way out teaches you to distrust it, and I would rather it simply left.

Your save states still load​

The save-state format did not change. Game Mode is a new way of pressing the same keys, so every save state written by the earlier releases loads normally.

This one matters more than the feature does. A release that quietly changes the format leaves a generation of slots unopenable, and the honest way to change a format is to change it loudly, with a version bump, when it really changes.

The documentation caught up​

The user guide gained a chapter on the gamepad, the technical reference gained the gamepad section and the real key path, and the interrupt map gained a case study of a finger that becomes a DOS keystroke.

And every box-drawing diagram in the documentation is now an SVG with straight borders, so the boxes look the same in every renderer and in every font.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key, so it installs over the previous version in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.15

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.15.apk
size:   16 500 506 bytes
sha256: dbf776abe6b69541194fa5bded5d2c807a94add4733a74ea2620b03227263f42

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository, and the Game Mode chapter there is the real reference — including what the buttons do when you have remapped them. Please read that rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work, and Game Mode is a thin layer on top of that. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input — and now the gamepad too, since it is the same events all the way down.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

A thumb can hold a direction, a button and a ball at the same time. The game, written in 1994, never has to know the difference.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.16：返回键又活了
item.content:encoded:
那个不动的按键​

你在游戏里，想退出。你按返回键。

什么也没发生。

你又按了一下，更用力一点，像是手机能被你说服似的。什么也没发生。启动器还开着，或者手柄还开着，或者键盘还杵在屏幕上；想出这个应用，只剩厂家放在屏幕上的那个手势——长滑，得有人手把手教一遍的那种。

从 Android 13 开始，这个返回键就一直是这样。从 1.0.0.9 到 1.0.0.15，每一个版本都是这样。这是我这个应用历史上最老、也最扎手的一个版本，而我好几个月都没注意到，因为我总是两只拇指捧着手机，脸贴着屏幕。

这一版，返回键又活过来了。

到底发生了什么​

要出这个毛病，得两件事同时出错。

Android 13 里，系统不再把返回键送给 Activity了。返回变成了一种手势，交给分发器处理，老路径——onKeyDown()、onBackPressed()——从此再也不会因为它被调用。这是故意的：系统只想要一套手势模型，不要两套。

而 WhereQ-DOSBox 是个 SDL 应用。SDL2 的 SDLActivity 负责处理按键事件，而且对每一个都返回 true，因为 SDL 就是要看到键盘。画面就是游戏本身。于是按键进了 SDL，SDL 说了声"收到"，Activity 什么也没听见。

两件事凑在一起，按键被送到了、被吃掉了、然后掉在地上。从用户这边看，这和手机按键坏了没有任何区别。

修法是：不要再要那个键，去要那个手势。应用向系统注册一个 OnBackInvokedCallback——Android 自己为这件事引入的 API——返回手势就直接到了应用手里，由应用来决定它意味着什么。

有一个坑值得点出来，因为它是最容易想到的错答案。Android 文档里写了一个退出的开关：manifest 里的 android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false"，让应用退回老路径。那不是修法。老路径恰恰是 SDL 会吃掉按键的那条路——它把 SDL 吞掉的那个键事件又请回来了。更糟的是，到 Android 16，系统连注册过的回调也不理了，于是退出这个开关等于把两条路都断了。

所以这个开关不能有。有一条单元测试专门去读 manifest，只要这个属性回来就让构建失败。

按屏幕上真实的顺序退出去​

改这块的时候，我顺手发现顺序也是错的。

返回键应该把你一级一级地退出应用，而这些东西是叠着的：游戏启动器画在键盘上面，手柄画在键盘上面，键盘面板又折在手柄下面。返回应该先关掉最上面那一个。

它没有。第一次按下去折起了那个收起来的面板，手柄还站在原地——于是你得按第二次，才能从你正想离开的游戏里出来。

所以现在这个决定变成了一张表，而且每台设备上的表都是同一张：

启动器开着？        → 关掉启动器
手柄在屏幕上？      → 回到键盘
键盘面板展开着？    → 折起来
什么都没开？        → 离开应用

开着的东西按一次退一层，顺序就是你眼睛看到的顺序。它长得像一张表，因为它就是一张表——一个纯函数 resolveBackAction()，里面一点 Android 都没有，于是 JVM 可以测它：

:app:testDebugUnitTest          7 tests, 0 failures

而且"应用能收到返回手势"这句话说的是系统分发器，所以还有第二层测试需要真机：五个仪器测试通过系统的输入通道按下真正的返回键——像拇指那样按，而不是直接调 Activity——然后检查启动器确实关了、应用没被顺手退出，以及授权页面确实写着它承诺的东西。

需要 16 KB 页的设备​

Android 15 改了 64 位设备上的页大小。改的不是应用申请的页大小，是内核用来映射应用的那一层。一个加载段只按 4 KB 对齐、没按 16 KB 对齐的库，在这种设备上根本加载不进去。

DOSBox 是个 1990 年代的程序，链着 SDL2 和一个音乐库，它的 .so 是按 32 位 Android 的老规矩对齐的，此后没人再检查过。

现在对齐了。libdosbox.so 在三个 ABI 下的每一个 PT_LOAD 段都按 16 KB 对齐，CI 会读它构建出来的每一个库的头部，只要有一个没对齐就让构建失败。每一次 push 都跑的检查，比只跑过一次的检查值钱。

那个一直按着的鼠标键​

Game Mode 里有一个 DRAG 键：按住它，左键就一直是按下的状态，这样实时读鼠标的游戏能看见"键按着"，拖动也能一直拖。

如果你在 DRAG 锁着的时候离开 Game Mode，那个键会留在 DOSBox 里面。游戏那边还在看见一个没人按着的左键——一个选不中的结束、一个停不下来的拖拽，直到你碰巧又碰了一下屏幕。

现在这个锁会和按键、和其它鼠标键一起被释放：手柄离开屏幕、或者配置文件换了的时候都放。DRAG 锁是手柄的状态，不是机器的状态，它不再漏进机器里。

授权书跟着应用一起走​

这一条不是 bug，是一份义务，而我之前一直拿错了方式。

WhereQ-DOSBox 内嵌了 DOSBox 内核，它是 GPLv2。GPLv2 对程序本身（而不只是源码树）提了两个要求：授权书和版权声明必须跟着二进制走；每个拿到程序的人都必须能拿到完整的对应源码。

第二件是做到了——源码在 GitHub 上，授权页面里也有链接。第一件没有：GPL 正文和声明在仓库里，在 COPYING 和 NOTICE 里，仅此而已。装上 APK 的用户没有任何办法读到他所受约束的那份授权。

所以现在它们在应用里了。完整的 GPL v2 正文和 NOTICE——DOSBox 的署名、Em-DOSBox 的导入说明、SDL2 的 zlib 声明、商标声明——都打包在 APK 里，启动器的页脚就挨着版本号链过去：

授权页面。授权书和声明是从 assets 里读的，所以完全不需要网络。

仓库根目录的 NOTICE 也补上了它一直缺的 SDL2 声明——zlib 授权要求这份声明随链接了 SDL2 的二进制一起走，而这个二进制确实链接了它。

拿它​

Release APK 用发布密钥签名，所以可以直接覆盖安装上一版：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — 标签 v1.0.0.16

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.16.apk
size:   16 510 058 bytes
sha256: 183f16ee3fd219a878b56b6a08758a184370b834a0fef63b63a7aea7f4faa773

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，Android 5.0 及更新，完全离线，不要账号，不做追踪。项目是 GPL-2.0，DOSBox 内核连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和每个文件的头部声明一起嵌入——从这一版起，授权书本身也在里面。

**你的存档照样读得动。**存档格式一点没变。

再说一遍：**这篇文章不是文档。**文档是仓库，而且是一份单一的技术参考文档，不是一堆零散笔记。请去读它，而不是只听我说。

谢谢，DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 是由 DOSBox Team 写下的——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一个操作系统做成了此后世界上造出来的每台机器都能跑的东西，包括那些还没造出来的机器。他们让它活了三十年，然后送给了任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创性、手艺和慷慨全都属于他们。

这个移植建立在 Em-DOSBox 之上——Boris Gjenero 用 Emscripten 做的 DOSBox r4305 构建，它源自 Ismail Khatib 第一次尝试用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox，也站在 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作之上。窗口、音频和触摸输入由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；本移植与 DOSBox 团队无隶属关系，也未得到其认可。

一个不动的按键比一个没有的按键更糟，因为你就是会一直按下去。如果你装了这个应用之后，返回键一直不理你——这就是你要的那一版。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.16: the back button works again
item.content:encoded:
The button that stopped working​

You are in a game. You want out. You press Back.

Nothing happens.

You press it again, harder, as if the phone could be persuaded. Nothing happens. The launcher stays open, or the gamepad stays open, or the keyboard stays up, and the only way out of the app is the gesture that the manufacturer put on the screen — the long swipe, the thing you have to be taught.

That is what the Back button has been doing since Android 13, in every release from 1.0.0.9 to 1.0.0.15. It is the oldest release in this app's life and the one with the sharpest edges, and I did not notice it for months, because I use the phone with two thumbs and my face to the screen.

This release is the one where the Back button works again.

What actually happened​

Two things had to go wrong, and they had to go wrong together.

In Android 13 the system stopped sending the back key to the activity. The back press became a gesture, handed to a dispatcher, and the old paths — onKeyDown(), onBackPressed() — stopped being called for it at all. That was deliberate: the system wanted one gesture model, not two.

And WhereQ-DOSBox is an SDL app. SDL2's SDLActivity handles the key events and returns true for every one of them, because SDL wants to see the keyboard. The surface is the game. So the key went to SDL, SDL said "handled", and the activity never heard about it.

Put the two together and you get a button that is delivered, consumed, and dropped on the floor. From the user's side there is no difference between that and a broken phone.

The fix is to stop asking for the key and start asking for the gesture. The app registers an OnBackInvokedCallback with the system — the API Android itself introduced for this — and the back gesture comes to the app directly, where the app can decide what it means.

One trap is worth naming, because it is the obvious wrong answer. Android documents an opt-out: android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false" in the manifest, which puts the app back on the legacy path. That is not a fix. The legacy path is precisely the path SDL breaks — it restores the key event that SDL eats. Worse, on Android 16 the system then also ignores a registered callback, so opting out loses both ways of reaching the app.

So the opt-out stays out. There is a unit test that reads the manifest and fails the build if that attribute ever comes back.

Back, in the order things are actually on screen​

While I was in there, I noticed the order was wrong.

The Back press has to walk you back out of the app, one thing at a time, and the things are stacked: the game launcher is drawn on top of the keyboard, the gamepad is drawn on top of the keyboard, the keyboard panel folds under the gamepad. Back should close the topmost thing first.

It did not. The first press folded the hidden panel and left the gamepad standing, so the second press was needed to get out of the game you were trying to leave.

So the decision is now one table, and the table is now the same on every device:

launcher open?        → close the launcher
game mode on screen?  → back to the keyboard
keyboard panel out?   → fold the panel
nothing open?         → leave the app

One press per thing, in the order you can see them. It reads like a table because it is a table — one pure function, resolveBackAction(), with no Android in it at all, which means the JVM can test it:

:app:testDebugUnitTest          7 tests, 0 failures

And because "the app handles the back gesture" is a claim about a system dispatcher, there is a second layer of test that needs a real device: five instrumented tests that press the actual back button through the system input pipeline — the way a thumb does, not by calling the activity — and check that the launcher closes, that the app stays alive while it is open, and that the licence screen carries what it claims to carry.

The devices that need 16 KB pages​

Android 15 changed the page size on 64-bit devices. Not the size of the pages the app asks for — the size of the pages the kernel uses to map the app. A library whose loadable segments are aligned to 4 KB but not to 16 KB simply will not load on such a device.

DOSBox is a 1990s program that links SDL2 and a music library; its .so was aligned the way 32-bit Android wanted, and nothing had checked since.

It is aligned now. Every PT_LOAD segment of libdosbox.so is aligned to 16 KB in all three ABIs, and CI reads the ELF headers of every library it builds and fails the build if one of them is not. A check that runs on every push is worth more than a check that ran once.

The mouse button that stayed down​

Game Mode has a DRAG button: hold it and the left mouse button stays down, so a game that reads the mouse live sees a held button and a drag keeps dragging.

If you left Game Mode while DRAG was locked, the button stayed down inside DOSBox. The game kept seeing a left button that nobody was holding — a selection that would not end, a drag that would not stop, until you happened to touch the screen again.

The lock is released now, together with the keys and the other buttons, whenever the gamepad goes away or the profile changes. The DRAG lock is a state of the gamepad, not of the machine, and it no longer leaks into the machine.

The licence travels with the app​

This one is not a bug. It is an obligation, and I had been carrying it the wrong way.

WhereQ-DOSBox embeds the DOSBox core, which is GPLv2. GPLv2 asks two things of the program, not only of the source tree: the licence and the copyright notices have to travel with the binary, and every recipient has to be able to get the complete corresponding source.

The second one was fine — the source is on GitHub, and the licence screen links to it. The first one was not: the GPL text and the notices were in the repository, in COPYING and NOTICE, and nowhere else. A user who installed the APK had no way to read the licence they were bound by.

So they are in the app now. The full GPL v2 text and the NOTICE — the DOSBox attribution, the Em-DOSBox import, the SDL2 zlib notice, the trademark note — travel inside the APK, and the launcher's footer links to them, next to the version:

The licence screen. The licence and the notices are read from the assets, so they work with no network at all.

The NOTICE at the repository root also gained the SDL2 notice it was missing, because the zlib licence requires that notice to travel with the binary that links SDL2 — and the binary does.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key, so it installs over the previous version in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.16

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.16.apk
size:   16 510 058 bytes
sha256: 183f16ee3fd219a878b56b6a08758a184370b834a0fef63b63a7aea7f4faa773

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact — and, as of this release, so is the licence itself.

Your save states still load. Nothing about the save format changed.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository, and it is a single reference document rather than a folder of notes. Please read that rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

A button that does nothing is worse than a button that is missing, because you keep pressing it. If Back has been ignoring you since you installed the app — this is the release you want.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.14：超时的存档不再替下一次请求作答
item.content:encoded:
你按了两次存档​

你正和一个大块头打得难解难分，按下 Save。

什么也没回来。档位没填上，转圈也没转，手机忙了大概一秒——长到你又按了一次 Save，因为刚才那一下显然没生效。

第二次确实生效了，它存下来了。可问题正在这里：落到磁盘上的那个文件，不一定是第二次按键想要的那个文件。

这就是 1.0.0.14 的全部内容。它是一次修补版，含三处修复，全在存档的内部管路上，而且完全不改动存档文件本身。

存档面板。这一版发生的所有事情，都发生在这几个档位的背后。

迟到的答案会去回答下一个问题​

应用并不直接驱动模拟器核心。它把事情交出去——存这个状态、读那个状态——答案再从一条通道里回来。存和读都有时间上限，因为一个不再回话的核不能把手机一直挂住。

一旦某个请求超了时，它就被放弃了。可核心并不知道这件事。它照样把活干完，照样把结果递回来——递进那个位置，而那里已经坐着一个新的请求在等。

于是，下一次存档拿到了上一次存档的回答。应用被告知新的存档已经完成。而磁盘上的那个文件，是那个旧请求写下的文件。

现在每个请求都带一个代次编号。一个在它所属的请求已经放弃之后才抵达的完成通知，会被直接丢掉：它属于一个早已不存在的请求。

一个文件的两个名字​

第二处修复更老，也更安静。DOS 程序可以用 INT 21h/45h 复制一个文件句柄，从那一刻起，这个文件就有两个名字、一份身份。

读档会把机器还原成原样，所以这两个名字也得原样回来，像从前那样共用同一个文件。现在就是这样：引用计数会按存档时的样子回去。

以前这个计数经不起这一趟。关掉其中一个名字，另一个会跟着一起倒——那一次关闭把共享文件的引用计数带到了零，活下来的那个名字于是变成 "invalid handle"。

一直没关掉的那个文件描述符​

第三处修复关于读档替换掉的那台机器。读入一个状态，就是把正在跑的机器扔掉，再用文件里的内容造一台新的。旧的那台必须关掉，而关掉它就得把它手上的文件也关掉——手机上真正的文件，不是客机系统自己以为的那些。

以前，如果一个状态里存在共享句柄，每读一次档就会留下一个宿主机文件描述符不关。不是崩溃，也不是错误的答案：是一个描述符，会在这次会话剩下的时间里一直开着，每读一次档就多一个，直到应用退出。

现在被丢弃的那台机器会被正确关掉，无论它的引用计数是多少。

你的存档还是读得出来​

存档格式没有改动。 三处修复都在快照的内部管路上，不在文件里，所以之前各版本写下的存档都照常读得出来。

这一点值得大声说出来，因为读者真正在意的正是它：一次悄悄改掉状态格式的发布，会在你身后留下一排再也打不开的档位。

同一条线的另一头​

Resume 按钮会读回你上次玩的那个游戏的最新档位，而且会告诉你它要干什么：Resume whereq-demo-bundle · slot 1 · just now。

一个替别的请求作答的存档，偏偏是在这里没人看得出来，偏偏在这里让你赔上一个晚上。

存档之后的 Files 面板。Resume 按钮，以及那行写着它要读哪个档位的字。

文档也长了一大截​

同一版还把两份文档带进了仓库：一份中断对照表——模拟器里的每一个 INT 是什么用途、由哪段代码应答；一份用户指南，配着它自己用的截图，把整个应用走了一遍。仓库的文档一下子厚了很多。

如果你对这个应用还很陌生，用户指南值得一读。如果你属于那种想知道模拟器拿 INT 21h 怎么办的人，中断对照表也值得一读。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装上一版：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.14

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.14.apk
size:   16 482 965 bytes
sha256: 2bf4d58b8e59413fa1795f7a2baa65b13f642daa76d9696a062d70893ad2d628

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

签名证书的 SHA-256 是 b16b480d5a1ff6d35baff0b15fa3fc4b0ee815e500861fbff1b062c9bf7d3933。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身——用户指南、中断对照表和技术参考。请去读它们，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

一个回答了你没问的问题的模拟器，不是慢，而是错；而这种错会推迟出现，出现在一个你根本没存过的存档里。这一版让迟到的答案死在半路上。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.14: a save that timed out no longer answers the next request
item.content:encoded:
You pressed Save twice​

You were halfway through a fight with something large. You pressed Save.

Nothing came back. The slot did not fill, the spinner did not spin, and the phone was busy for a second — long enough that you pressed Save again, because the first press clearly had not registered.

The second press did register. It saved. And that was the problem: the file that went to disk was not necessarily the file that the second press asked for.

That is the whole of 1.0.0.14. It is a patch release with three repairs, all of them in the save-state plumbing, and it changes nothing about the save file itself.

The save-state sheet. Everything in this release happens behind these three slots.

A late answer used to answer the next question​

The app does not drive the emulator core directly. It asks it to do things — save this state, restore that state — and the answer comes back through a channel. A save or a restore has a time limit, because a core that has stopped answering must not hang the phone forever.

When one overran its limit, the request was given up on. But the core did not know that. It finished the work anyway, and handed its result back — into the place where the next request was already waiting.

So the next save got the previous save's answer. The app was told that the new save was done. The file on disk was the file the old request wrote.

Every request now carries a generation number. A completion that arrives after its own request gave up is dropped: it belongs to a request that no longer exists.

Two names for one file​

The second repair is older and quieter. A DOS program can duplicate a file handle with INT 21h/45h, and from that moment on the file has two names and one identity.

A restore puts the machine back exactly as it was, so the two names have to come back too, sharing one file the way they shared it before. That is what happens now: the reference count goes back as it was saved.

Before, the count did not survive the trip. Close one of the two names and the other went down with it — the close took the shared file's reference count to zero, and the surviving name became "invalid handle".

The descriptor that stayed open​

The third repair is about the machine a restore replaces. Loading a state throws the running machine away and builds a new one from the file. The old one has to be closed, and closing it has to close the files it holds — the real files on the phone, not the guest's idea of them.

Before, a state in which a handle was shared left one host file descriptor open on every restore. Not a crash, not a wrong answer: a descriptor that stayed open for the rest of the session, one per restore, until the app was closed.

Now the discarded machine is closed properly, whatever its reference count.

Your save states still load​

The save-state format did not change. All three fixes are in the snapshot's plumbing, not in the file, so every save state written by the earlier releases loads normally.

That is worth saying out loud, because it is the part readers actually care about: a release that quietly re-cut the state format would leave a shelf of unopenable slots behind it.

The other end of the same line​

The Resume button restores the newest slot of the last game you played, and it tells you what it is about to do — Resume whereq-demo-bundle · slot 1 · just now.

A save that answers for the wrong request is exactly the kind of thing nobody notices there, and exactly the kind of thing that costs you an evening.

The Files panel after a save. The Resume button and the line that says which slot it will restore.

The documentation grew too​

The same release brought two documents into the repository: an interrupt map — every INT in the emulator, what it is for, and which code answers it — and a user guide that walks through the app with the screenshots it uses. The repository's documentation grew a great deal.

The guide is worth having if the app is new to you. The interrupt map is worth having if you are the kind of person who wants to know what the emulator does with INT 21h.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key, so it installs over the previous version in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.14

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.14.apk
size:   16 482 965 bytes
sha256: 2bf4d58b8e59413fa1795f7a2baa65b13f642daa76d9696a062d70893ad2d628

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

The signing certificate SHA-256 is b16b480d5a1ff6d35baff0b15fa3fc4b0ee815e500861fbff1b062c9bf7d3933.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository — the user guide, the interrupt map and the technical reference. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

An emulator that answers a question you did not ask is not slow — it is wrong, and the wrongness turns up later, in a save you never made. This release lets the late answer die on the way out.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 的中断地图：模拟器里每一个 INT 都在干什么
item.content:encoded:
所有 DOS 程序唯一都认同的那一个接口​

有一件事是我没料到自己会在意，然后一旦在意就停不下来的。

1987 年的 DOS 游戏并不知道显卡是什么。它不知道鼠标存在，也不知道键盘有个缓冲区。它只认一件事：往栈里推一个数，执行 INT，机器就会回答。INT 10h，机器把一个字符画到屏幕上。INT 16h，机器交出一个按键。INT 33h，机器告诉你鼠标在哪、哪些按钮按着。

契约就这么多。1991 到 1994 年的每一个游戏都是照着它写的，而且它从来没有变过。

为了写这篇文章，我把 DOSBox 的中断层认真读了一遍。它是整个模拟器里建得最用心的部分之一——同时也是这个移植版被迫想得最多的部分之一，因为触摸屏不是鼠标，手机也不是 PC。

所以，地图在这里。

地图​

向量服务用途
10h视频 BIOS文本与图形输出、光标、调色板、VESA/VBE
13h磁盘 BIOS对磁盘镜像做扇区读写
16h键盘 BIOS从 BIOS 键盘缓冲区取按键
21hDOSDOS API：文件、目录、内存、程序
29h快速控制台完全不走 DOS 层的字符输出
2Ah网络重定向器「有没有网络协议栈？」
2EhDOS shell模拟器自己的命令行
2Fh多路复用XMS、CD-ROM 等扩展的派发口
33h鼠标DOS 鼠标驱动
67hEMS扩展内存，以及 VCPI
74hPS/2 鼠标IRQ 12，鼠标的硬件向量
41h / 46h磁盘参数表磁盘的几何参数
1Fh / 43h / 44h字体8×8 字模块
4Bh虚拟 DMAVDMA 通道 API
73hIPX ESRNovell 网络事件服务例程

硬件那一侧有个容易搞混的点：IRQ 号不是向量号。两片 8259 各自有一个向量基址——主片 0x08，从片 0x70——向量是在中断被响应的那一刻才算出来的：

IRQ向量设备
008hPIT 定时器
109h键盘
20Ah到从片 PIC 的级联
60EhPCjr 键盘
870h实时时钟
1274hPS/2 鼠标
3、4、5、7、10、110Bh、0Ch、0Dh、0Fh、72h、73h其余全部——被屏蔽并记录在案

每个向量下面的功能码表，仓库里有一份完整版：docs/INTERRUPTS.md。这篇文章讲的是它背后的故事。

INT 10h 的一次调用，怎么变成了一个 C 函数​

DOSBox 里没有一张集中的中断表。服务安装自己的方式，和真 BIOS 一模一样：写中断向量表，让向量指向一段桩代码。

INT n 执行 0xCD 这条指令，落进 CPU_Interrupt()，CPU 压入标志、CS 和 EIP，关掉中断标志，再从 IVT 的 base + (n << 2) 处读出新的 CS:IP。这是货真价实的 8086 流程，DOSBox 一步步照做——来宾的栈上得到的六个字节，和真硬件上完全一样。

向量指向的并不是处理程序，而是一段桩：几字节手工拼出来的 16 位实模式代码，形状由一个回调类型决定。DOSBox 的巧思是一字节的合成操作码——FE 38——CPU 解释器认得它，把它变成一次对已注册 C 函数的调用。

这些桩不是装饰，它们的形状就是行为本身：

  • INT 16h 会空转。 桩是 IRET，然后十二个 NOP，再跳回回调。缓冲区里没有按键时，处理程序给 IP 加一，正好落回那串 NOP 上。于是来宾就在实模式里空转，直到 IRQ 1 送来一个按键——和真硬件一模一样。
  • INT 21h 要交税。 它的桩里含一条 loop 指令：模拟出来的 DOS 服务开销，一次调用几百个周期，8086 上本来也要花掉的。
  • INT 13h 用 BIOS 的方式报错。 桩的结尾是 IRET，然后 INT 0Eh，再 IRET——就是经典的「用 AL=0 调 INT 0Eh」磁盘错误约定。

INT 33h，以及为什么「点击」必须是「按住」​

鼠标是最有意思的一个，也是这个移植版改动最多的一个。

INT 33h 是一个对 AX 的 switch，实现了 35 个功能码。这里真正要紧的是两个：AX=03h，返回光标位置和按键状态；AX=0Ch，登记游戏自己的事件回调。

关于 AX=03h，有一点是我读到代码才真正明白的。mouse.buttons 是一个电平，不是边沿。Mouse_ButtonPressed() 置位，Mouse_ButtonReleased() 清位，AX=03h 把这个掩码原样交回去：

case 0x03:	/* Return Position and Button Status */
    reg_bx=mouse.buttons;
    reg_cx=POS_X;
    reg_dx=POS_Y;
    break;

每帧轮询 AX=03h 的游戏，问的是「这个按钮现在按着吗」，而不是「刚才有没有点一下」。

就这一个事实，决定了整个触摸层的设计。

从一根手指到一只 DOS 鼠标​

这个移植版的第一版做法很直白：手指按下就是 press，手指抬起就是 release，敲一下算一次点击。

这是错的。而且错在一种只有游戏才会暴露的地方。三国志英杰传的战斗界面读的是实时按键状态。如果按下和抬起落在它两次轮询之间，游戏根本看不见这次点击。光标动了，敲击等于没发生，玩家只会觉得这个应用坏了。

所以现在手指在玻璃上按多久，按钮就按住多久：

  SDL_FINGERDOWN        →  Mouse_ButtonPressed(0)   // 左键，按住
  SDL_FINGERMOTION      →  移动光标，按键仍然按着
  SDL_FINGERUP          →  Mouse_ButtonReleased(0)

敲一下于是变成一次真正的「按住再松开」的点击。拖动也变成真正的拖动——因为光标是在按键按着的时候移动的。

画面两侧的两块键盘区。整块屏幕就是那只鼠标。

吞掉每一次点击的那个陷阱​

还有第二个 bug，而且更古怪。DOSBox 在全屏时会「捕获鼠标」，这会置上 sdl.mouse.locked。这个标志一置上，Mouse_CursorMoved() 就忽略绝对位置，只累加相对位移。

在桌面上这是对的——被捕获的鼠标本来就是相对设备。可手机上根本没有鼠标可捕获，后果就是每一次敲击都被忽略，光标卡在屏幕正中。

修之前和修之后的实测：

点 (700, 300)点 (1500, 800)点 (1000, 500)
之前320, 100320, 100320, 100
之后97, 55453, 148231, 92

数字是精确的：0.153 × 80 × 8 = 97——DOS 文本屏 80 × 25 个字符格，每格 8 像素。原本永远落在同一个错误格子上的点击，现在落在你真正按下的地方。

右键​

DOS 鼠标有两个按钮，触摸屏只有一个。而绝大多数 DOS 游戏里右键是取消或返回，所以丢掉右键就是丢掉了一整类交互。

这里没有长按手势，也没有上下文菜单。右键由两个机制送出，而且两个都是按住式按钮，和左键完全一样：

  • 画面上的第二根手指。左键会先松开，所以两个按钮不会重叠；右键一直按到那根手指抬起。
  • 屏幕上的 RMB 键，在左边那块、紧挨 Tab。它通过 JNI 桥往 DOSBox 的事件队列里推一个真正的 SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT 的 SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN，事件走的路径和普通鼠标点击一模一样。

第二个机制有意思的地方在于，它压根不是一个手势——它是另一个事件类型，被塞进模拟器本来就在读的那个队列。

驱动的状态住在来宾内存之外​

这是我把存档格式重写了两次的那个 bug 的根子。

INT 33h 驱动的状态住在一个宿主的文件内静态结构体里，不在模拟出来的内存中。其中有三样东西，来宾在读档之后没法自己重建：

  • 游戏用 AX=0Ch 登记的事件回调——段、偏移和事件掩码；
  • AX=09h 定义的图形光标和它的热点；
  • 光标范围、位置、可见性和灵敏度。

少了第一样，症状精确得让人难受：光标还在动——那是 DOSBox 在画——但游戏的点击送不到游戏里。对话框的确认按钮就是没反应。模拟器看起来活蹦乱跳，游戏却是聋的。

少了第二样，光标退回默认的白色方块、热点归零，于是看得见的光标和真正的点击点对不上，敲击会落在目标的偏上偏左。

所以鼠标驱动必须成为存档的一部分。第一次尝试存了整个结构体。

结果把游戏卡死了。 三国志英杰传在读档时挂起，而且过一分钟就再也不响应点击——事件队列在一个卡住的 in_UIR 标志后面堆满了。把过期的队列和过期的 in_UIR 喂回中断处理程序，就是把垃圾喂给了游戏自己的回调。

修法是搞懂两种状态的分别：

配置值得保存，运行期状态是毒药。

最终形态存的是一个专门的 MouseStateBlock，只放来宾重建不了的东西——回调三元组、光标范围与位置、热点、光标掩码、灵敏度。读档时则把所有易失的部分重置：事件队列、按键与点击计数器、重入标志、光标绘制的背景缓冲。

还有一条规则，这是「宿主指针」规则的小号版本：结构体里有两个指向光标位图的宿主指针。它们从不写进文件，而是在读档后根据保存的光标类型重新推导：用户自定义的图形光标用恢复出来的掩码，其余一律用内置箭头。

同一条规则，往下一层：PIC​

中断控制器是同一个形状的问题，而这个移植版得出了同一个答案。

存档是机器的快照，而机器包含它的中断子系统。PIC_SaveState 和 PIC_LoadState 会把两个控制器结构体写进去——然后加载器故意不把全部都恢复：

	/* Keep the game's interrupt MASK and configuration, but drop any stale
	 * pending/in-service state: a restored in-service bit would block all
	 * lower-priority IRQs (so the RTC that drives INT 15h/86h, and thus sound
	 * timing, would stall), and a stale request bit would fire a spurious IRQ.
	 * At the top-of-main-loop restore point no IRQ is genuinely mid-service. */
	pics[i].imrr = ~pics[i].imr;
	pics[i].irr = 0;
	pics[i].isr = 0;

掩码是配置——来宾自己决定要哪些中断，它要留下来。在服务位和请求位是瞬态——一个残留的在服务位会卡死整个优先级链，一个残留的请求位会打出一次莫名的中断。

保留配置，丢掉运行期状态。同一句话，在两个不同的子系统里说了两遍，而两次都是靠撞墙撞出来的。

格式版本也随着设计在动：8 是「整个鼠标驱动状态」，9 是「精简成回调 + 范围 + 位置」，10 是「光标形状、热点和其余配置」。含义变了的格式必须把版本号喊出来，这样旧的存档会被拒绝，而不是被误读。

这个移植版没有改的东西​

这个答案更让人意外，也更值得直说：BIOS 中断层是上游代码。

src/ints/ 下的每一个文件自导入以来都没动过，只有一个例外。mouse.cpp 有五个导入之后的提交；而 int10.cpp 及其八个兄弟、bios.cpp、bios_disk.cpp、bios_keyboard.cpp、ems.cpp、xms.cpp 一个都没有。

DOS 层也一样。src/dos/dos.cpp——整个 INT 21h 处理程序——以及 dos_misc.cpp、dos_classes.cpp、dos_memory.cpp 与导入的源码逐字节相同。这个移植版对它的唯一侵入是一行，而且和中断没有关系：

SegSet16(ds,pspseg);SegSet16(es,pspseg);
/* WhereQ: a guest program has taken over the machine, so the boot
 * is over and a save-state request may be serviced. The shell
 * itself never reaches its prompt in this case (it is blocked
 * inside the program it started), so this is the only place where
 * the save-state module learns that the guest is running. */
SAVESTATE_GuestReady();

连包启动器都是走的标准路径。每个游戏会生成一个 RUN.BAT，被追加到模拟器的 [autoexec] 里；来宾随后用 INT 21h AH=4Bh 去 exec 它，再 AH=4Bh 跑游戏自己的 PLAY.BAT，最后 AH=4Ch 退出。这个移植版没有新增任何启动器 API——它只是挑了一个文件名，剩下的交给 DOS。

整个移植版大致就是这个形状：真正有意思的工作几乎从不在 BIOS 层，而在它上面那一层——把一根手指变成一只鼠标，把一次轻触变成一个按住不松的按钮，把一个游戏变成存档能带走的东西。

自己看一遍​

看这一层工作，最省事的办法是打开 MOUSE 日志分组，在 dosbox.conf 里：

[log]
logfile=/sdcard/dosbox.log
mouse=true

Android 应用不带 [log] 段，所以默认是关的。打开之后，驱动没有实现的每一次 INT 33h 调用都会被报出来：

Mouse Function 0018 not implemented!

这等于直接读出了游戏在要什么、驱动又没回答什么。再往前一个函数的地方，有一行被注释掉的日志，会打印每一次 INT 33h 调用的 AX、BX、CX 和光标位置——对想读这份代码的人来说，这是这个树里最值得解开的一行。

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox——源码、完整的中断地图 docs/INTERRUPTS.md，以及背后的技术参考。

致谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植版基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植版与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

模拟器就是一台由「对还没人问过的问题的回答」造出来的机器。真正有意思的工作，在于决定那个问题从一根拇指上传来时，回答应该是什么。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox interrupts: the map of every INT in the emulator
item.content:encoded:
The one interface every DOS program agrees on​

Here is something I did not expect to care about, and then could not stop caring about.

A DOS game from 1987 does not know what a graphics card is. It does not know that a mouse exists, or that a keyboard has a buffer. It knows exactly one thing: it can ask the machine a question by pushing a number onto the stack and executing INT. INT 10h and the machine will put a character on the screen. INT 16h and the machine will hand over a keystroke. INT 33h and the machine will tell it where the mouse is and which buttons are down.

That is the whole contract. Every game from 1991 to 1994 is written against it, and it never changed.

I have been reading DOSBox's interrupt layer properly for this article, and it turns out to be one of the most carefully built parts of the emulator — and one of the parts this port has had to think about hardest, because a touch screen is not a mouse and a phone is not a PC.

So here is the map.

The map​

VectorServiceWhat it is for
10hVideo BIOStext and graphics output, the cursor, the palette, VESA/VBE
13hDisk BIOSsector reads and writes against the disk images
16hKeyboard BIOSkeystrokes out of the BIOS keyboard buffer
21hDOSthe DOS API: files, directories, memory, programs
29hFast consolecharacter output with no DOS overhead at all
2AhNetwork redirector"is there a network stack?"
2EhDOS shellthe emulator's own command shell
2FhMultiplexthe dispatcher for XMS, CD-ROM and other extensions
33hMousethe DOS mouse driver
67hEMSexpanded memory, and VCPI
74hPS/2 mouseIRQ 12, the mouse's hardware vector
41h / 46hDisk parameter tablesthe geometry of the disks
1Fh / 43h / 44hFontsthe 8×8 character blocks
4BhVirtual DMAthe VDMA channel API
73hIPX ESRthe Novell network event service routine

And the hardware side, where an IRQ number is not a vector number. The two 8259s have a vector base — 0x08 for the master, 0x70 for the slave — and the vector is computed when the interrupt is taken:

IRQVectorDevice
008hthe PIT timer
109hthe keyboard
20Ahthe cascade to the slave PIC
60Ehthe PCjr keyboard
870hthe real-time clock
1274hthe PS/2 mouse
3, 4, 5, 7, 10, 110Bh, 0Ch, 0Dh, 0Fh, 72h, 73heverything else — masked and recorded

The full map, with the function-code tables underneath each vector, is in the repository as docs/INTERRUPTS.md. This article is the story behind it.

How a call to INT 10h becomes a C function​

There is no central interrupt table in DOSBox. A service installs itself the way a real BIOS does: it writes the interrupt vector table, and the vector points at a stub.

INT n executes opcode 0xCD, lands in CPU_Interrupt(), and the CPU pushes flags, CS and EIP, clears the interrupt flag, and reads the new CS:IP out of the IVT at base + (n << 2). That is the real 8086 sequence, and DOSBox runs it for real — the guest's stack gets the same six bytes it would on hardware.

What the vector points at is not a handler but a stub: a few bytes of hand-assembled real-mode code whose shape is decided by a callback type. DOSBox's trick is a synthetic one-byte opcode — FE 38 — that the CPU interpreter recognises and turns into a call to a registered C function.

The stubs are not decoration. Their shape is the behaviour:

  • INT 16h spins. The stub is IRET, then twelve NOPs, then a jump back into the callback. When no key is buffered the handler adds one to IP, which lands it back on the NOP sled. The guest therefore spins in real mode until IRQ 1 delivers a key — exactly what real hardware does.
  • INT 21h pays a tax. Its stub contains a loop instruction: the emulated DOS service overhead, a few hundred cycles per call that a real 8086 would have spent.
  • INT 13h reports errors the BIOS way. Its stub ends with IRET, then INT 0Eh, then IRET — the classic "call INT 0Eh with AL=0" disk-error convention.

INT 33h, and why a click has to be a held button​

The mouse is the interesting one, and it is the one this port changed.

INT 33h is a switch on AX with 35 implemented function codes. The two that matter here are AX=03h, which returns the cursor position and the button state, and AX=0Ch, which registers the game's event callback.

Here is the thing about AX=03h that I did not appreciate until I read the code. mouse.buttons is a level, not an edge. Mouse_ButtonPressed() sets a bit; Mouse_ButtonReleased() clears it; AX=03h hands the mask straight back:

case 0x03:	/* Return Position and Button Status */
    reg_bx=mouse.buttons;
    reg_cx=POS_X;
    reg_dx=POS_Y;
    break;

A game that polls AX=03h every frame is asking "is the button down right now?" — not "did a click happen?".

And that single fact determined the design of the touch layer.

From a finger to a DOS mouse​

The first version of this port did the obvious thing: a finger down was a press, a finger up was a release. A tap was a click.

That is wrong, and it was wrong in a way that only showed up in games. 三国志英杰传's battle UI reads the live button state. If the press and the release land between two of its polls, the game never sees the click. The cursor moves, the tap registers as nothing, and the player concludes the app is broken.

So the finger now holds the button down for exactly as long as it is on the glass:

  SDL_FINGERDOWN        →  Mouse_ButtonPressed(0)   // LEFT, held
  SDL_FINGERMOTION      →  move the cursor, button still held
  SDL_FINGERUP          →  Mouse_ButtonReleased(0)

A tap becomes a real held-then-released click. A drag becomes a real drag, because the cursor moves while the button is down.

The two pads, either side of the picture. The whole screen is the mouse.

The trap that ate every tap​

There was a second bug, and it was stranger. DOSBox captures the mouse when it goes fullscreen, which sets sdl.mouse.locked. With that flag set, Mouse_CursorMoved() ignores the absolute position and only accumulates relative movement.

On a desktop that is correct — a captured mouse is a relative device. On a phone there is no mouse to capture, and the consequence was that every tap was ignored and the cursor sat in the middle of the screen.

The measurement, before and after:

tap (700, 300)tap (1500, 800)tap (1000, 500)
before320, 100320, 100320, 100
after97, 55453, 148231, 92

The numbers are exact. 0.153 × 80 × 8 = 97 — the DOS text screen's 80 × 25 cells at 8 pixels each. A tap that was always landing on the same wrong cell now lands where you touched.

The right button​

A DOS mouse has two buttons. A touchscreen has one. And in most DOS games the right button is cancel or back, so losing it loses a whole category of interaction.

There is no long-press gesture and no context menu. Two mechanisms deliver it, and both are held buttons, exactly like the left one:

  • A second finger on the picture. The left button is released first, so the two never overlap, and the right button is held until that finger lifts.
  • The on-screen RMB key, next to Tab on the left pad. It pushes a real SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN for SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT into DOSBox's event queue through the JNI bridge, and the event flows through the same path as a mouse click.

The second one is the interesting one, because it is not a gesture at all. It is a different event type injected into the queue the emulator already reads.

The driver's state lives outside the guest's memory​

Here is the bug that made me rewrite the save-state format twice.

The INT 33h driver's state lives in a host file-static struct, not in the emulated memory. Three pieces of it cannot be rebuilt by the guest after a restore:

  • the event callback the game registered with AX=0Ch — the segment, the offset and the event mask;
  • the graphics cursor and its hotspot, from AX=09h;
  • the cursor range, the position, the visibility, the sensitivity.

Without the first, the symptom is precise and nasty: the cursor still moves — DOSBox draws it — but the game's clicks stop reaching the game. A dialog's confirm button simply does nothing. The emulator looks alive; the game is deaf.

Without the second, the cursor reverts to the default white block drawn with a zero hotspot, so the visible cursor no longer lines up with the real click point, and taps land up and to the left of the target.

So the mouse driver had to become part of the save state. The first attempt saved the whole struct.

That wedged the games. 三国志英杰传 hung on load, and stopped responding to clicks after a minute once the event queue filled behind a stuck re-entrancy flag. Feeding a stale event queue and a stale in_UIR back into the interrupt handler fed garbage into the game's own callback.

The fix was to learn the difference between two kinds of state:

Configuration is worth saving. Run-time state is poison.

The final form saves a dedicated MouseStateBlock holding only what the guest cannot rebuild — the callback triple, the cursor range and position, the hotspot, the cursor masks, the sensitivity. And on load it resets everything volatile: the event queue, the button and click counters, the re-entrancy flag, the cursor-draw backing store.

One more rule, and it is the host-pointer rule in miniature. The struct holds two host pointers — to the cursor bitmaps. They are never written to disk. They are re-derived from the saved cursor type after a load: a user-defined graphics cursor uses the restored masks, anything else uses the built-in arrow.

The same rule, one layer down: the PIC​

The interrupt controller has the same shape of problem, and the port reached the same answer.

A save state is a snapshot of a machine, and the machine includes its interrupt subsystem. PIC_SaveState and PIC_LoadState write the two controller structs — and then the loader deliberately does not restore all of it:

	/* Keep the game's interrupt MASK and configuration, but drop any stale
	 * pending/in-service state: a restored in-service bit would block all
	 * lower-priority IRQs (so the RTC that drives INT 15h/86h, and thus sound
	 * timing, would stall), and a stale request bit would fire a spurious IRQ.
	 * At the top-of-main-loop restore point no IRQ is genuinely mid-service. */
	pics[i].imrr = ~pics[i].imr;
	pics[i].irr = 0;
	pics[i].isr = 0;

The mask is the configuration — the guest's own decision about which interrupts it wants, and it survives. The in-service and request registers are transient — a leftover in-service bit wedges the priority chain, and a leftover request fires a spurious IRQ.

Keep the configuration. Drop the run-time state. The same sentence, twice, in two different subsystems, and both times it was learned by breaking it.

The format version moved as the design moved: 8 was "the whole mouse driver state", 9 was "slimmed to callback + range + position", 10 is "cursor shape, hotspot and the rest of the configuration". A format that changes meaning must change its version loudly, so that an older save is refused rather than misread.

What this port did not change​

The more surprising answer, and the one worth stating plainly: the BIOS interrupt layer is upstream code.

Every file in src/ints/ is untouched since the import, with one exception. mouse.cpp has five post-import commits; int10.cpp and its eight siblings, bios.cpp, bios_disk.cpp, bios_keyboard.cpp, ems.cpp and xms.cpp have none.

The same is true of the DOS layer. src/dos/dos.cpp — the whole INT 21h handler — dos_misc.cpp, dos_classes.cpp and dos_memory.cpp are byte-identical to the imported sources. The port's single intrusion into it is one line, and it is not about interrupts at all:

SegSet16(ds,pspseg);SegSet16(es,pspseg);
/* WhereQ: a guest program has taken over the machine, so the boot
 * is over and a save-state request may be serviced. The shell
 * itself never reaches its prompt in this case (it is blocked
 * inside the program it started), so this is the only place where
 * the save-state module learns that the guest is running. */
SAVESTATE_GuestReady();

Even the bundle launcher rides the stock path. Each game gets a generated RUN.BAT that is appended to the emulator's [autoexec]; the guest then does INT 21h AH=4Bh to exec it, AH=4Bh again for the game's own PLAY.BAT, and AH=4Ch to exit. The port did not add a launcher API. It chose a filename and let DOS do the rest.

That is the shape of the whole port: the interesting work is almost never in the BIOS layer. It is in what sits above it — turning a finger into a mouse, a tap into a held button, and a game into something a save state can carry.

Watching it yourself​

The cheapest way to see this layer work is the MOUSE log group, enabled from dosbox.conf:

[log]
logfile=/sdcard/dosbox.log
mouse=true

The Android app ships no [log] section, so it is off by default. Once it is on, every INT 33h call that the driver does not implement is reported:

Mouse Function 0018 not implemented!

which is a direct read-out of what a game is asking for and what the driver does not answer. There is a commented-out line one function away that would print the AX, BX, CX and cursor position of every INT 33h call — the single most useful change a developer could make to this tree.

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — the source, the full interrupt map at docs/INTERRUPTS.md, and the technical reference behind it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

An emulator is a machine made of answers to questions nobody has asked yet. The interesting work is in deciding what the answer should be when the question arrives from a thumb.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.13：读档之后，存档还记得自己是什么时候存的
item.content:encoded:
「刚刚」​

午饭之后你回来接着打。点那个写着「五小时前」的档位。游戏原样回来了——那只大家伙、血条、你当时站着的那个房间，都在你离开时的样子。

然后档位上写着的是「刚刚」。

存档还是你存的那一份，游戏还是你走时的那一刻。只有时间在说谎，而且它撒的方向刚好是让这个应用显得不可信：它唯一该记住的事，它自己没记住。

1.0.0.13 的全部内容就是这个。这是我发过的最小的一版，修复也只有三行。

存档面板。每个档位旁边的那一行字，就是这一版唯一要修的东西。

先说前提：存档已经搬到应用外面了​

这个 bug 得先说清楚存档放在哪儿才讲得通，因为 1.0.0.12 把它们搬走了，而那一版在这里一直没发过文章。简单交代一下。

在那之前，存档是应用私有目录里的一个文件。卸载应用——或者手机丢了、换手机了——所有存档跟着一起没。现在应用可以自己留一份在你手上的地方：在手机上选一个文件夹（Config → Saves folder，或者第一次存档之后弹出来的那个邀请），之后每个档位都会镜像到那里，压成 gzip，就放在游戏旁边。

  应用                              你选的那个文件夹
  ──────                          ────────────────────
  存档   ── gzip ──▶                STARFALL/
                                    slot1.gz
                                    slot2.gz
                                    bundle.zip      (游戏本身)

于是重装、换手机、或者手滑删了应用，东西都能回来：游戏按名字 offer 给你恢复，它们的存档已经在那里了。同名的两个压缩包会按名字区分——game 和 game (2)——所以它们的存档不会混到同一个地方。

Files 面板：游戏列表，以及设置存档目录的 Config 按钮。

而这次搬家，恰恰就是 bug 的来处。

错在哪一行​

本地那份档位不见了的时候——重装了、换手机了——应用会从镜像里把它重建出来。文件是新写出来的，于是带上了写的那一刻的时间戳。

启动器读的就是这个文件上的时间。于是五小时前存的档位，从镜像里恢复出来，就成了「刚刚」。

快照本身一点问题都没有，而且从来就没问题过：机器、声音芯片、DOS 文件句柄，全都原样回来了。错的只有那个标签。可这反而更糟，因为一个错的标签会让你开始怀疑底下的东西——你会怀疑这次恢复到底忠实不忠实，其实恢复完美无缺，撒谎的是日期。

修法是把时间跟着一块带过去。镜像知道这个档位究竟是什么时候存的，重建出来的本地文件现在拿到的就是这个时间，而不是当前时间：

// Keep the original SAVE time: restoring rewrites the local file, so
// without this the slot would show "just now" after every load.
if (ok) doc.lastModified().takeIf { it > 0L }?.let { local.setLastModified(it) }

一行活儿，一行代码，档位于是又变回「5 小时前」。

手机上的名字​

启动器名字、通知和桌面图标现在都带着这个项目自己的名字和标记：WhereQ-DOSBox。

包名是 com.whereq.dosbox，下载文件名是 whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.13.apk，所以这一版可以直接覆盖安装上一版——包名一样、签名密钥一样，不用先卸载。你的游戏和存档原地不动。

你的存档还是读得出来​

存档格式什么都没改。 修的是启动器，不是快照，所以之前各版本写下的存档都照常读得出来——文件布局仍然是版本 10，和当初把鼠标块精简成稳定配置之后那一版一样。

这比听起来更重要：一次悄悄改掉格式的发布，会留下一批再也打不开的存档。老实做法是——格式真变了就大声改，带版本号地改。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装上一版：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.13

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.13.apk
size:   16 482 792 bytes
sha256: 98243e5577276d31f89adc1ac776bfc4242fdc0ff43f877bc36797c138cffa94

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身，而且现在是一份参考文档，不再是一堆笔记。请去读那份，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

一个会谎报自己年龄的存档只是个小谎，而小谎正是工具失去信任的方式。如果你发现「继续」下面那个档位这一周一直写着「刚刚」——这一版就是你要的那一版。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.13: a restored save keeps the time it was made
item.content:encoded:
"Just now"​

You come back to the game after lunch. You tap the slot that said you saved it five hours ago. The game loads exactly where you left it — the boss, the health bar, the room you were in.

And the slot now says "just now".

The save is the save you made. The game is the game you left. Only the timestamp lies, and it lies in the direction that makes the app feel like it cannot be trusted with the one thing it is supposed to remember.

That is the whole of 1.0.0.13. It is the smallest release I have shipped and the only one where the fix is three lines long.

The save-state sheet. The line next to each slot is the only thing this release is about.

First, the ground moved: the saves live outside the app now​

The bug only makes sense once you know where the saves live, because 1.0.0.12 moved them and that release never got a post here. So, briefly.

Until then, a save state was a file in the app's own private storage. Uninstall the app — or lose the phone, or switch phones — and every save goes with it. The app can now keep a copy somewhere that is yours: pick a folder on the phone (Config → Saves folder, or the offer that appears after your first save), and every slot is mirrored there, gzipped, next to the game itself.

  the app                          the folder you picked
  ──────                          ────────────────────
  the slot   ── gzip ──▶             STARFALL/
                                     slot1.gz
                                     slot2.gz
                                     bundle.zip      (the game)

So a reinstall, a new phone, or an app deleted by accident all come back: the games are offered for restore by name, and their save states are already there. Two archives with the same file name are told apart by name — game and game (2) — so their saves never end up in the same place.

The Files panel: the games, and the Config button where the saves folder is set.

And that move is exactly where the bug comes from.

The line that was wrong​

When the local copy of a slot is gone — a reinstall, a new phone — the app rebuilds it from the mirror. It writes the file, and a written file has a fresh timestamp: the moment of the write.

The launcher reads the time off that file. So a slot made five hours ago, restored from the mirror, came back labelled "just now".

The snapshot itself was fine, and it was always fine: the machine, the sound chips, the DOS file handles, all of it came back exactly. Only the label was wrong. Which is worse in a way, because a wrong label makes you doubt the thing underneath it — you start wondering whether the restore was faithful, when the restore was perfect and the date was a lie.

The fix is to carry the time across with the state. The mirror knows when the slot was really saved; the rebuilt local file now gets that timestamp instead of the current one:

// Keep the original SAVE time: restoring rewrites the local file, so
// without this the slot would show "just now" after every load.
if (ok) doc.lastModified().takeIf { it > 0L }?.let { local.setLastModified(it) }

One line of work for one line of code, and the slot says "5 hours ago" again.

The name on the phone​

The launcher name, the notification and the launcher icons carry the project's own name and mark: WhereQ-DOSBox.

The package is com.whereq.dosbox and the download is whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.13.apk, so this release installs over the previous one in place — same package, same signing key, no uninstalling first. Your games and your saves stay where they are.

Your save states still load​

Nothing about the save format changed. The fix is in the launcher, not in the snapshot, so every save state written by the earlier releases loads normally — the file layout is still version 10, the same one that has been in use since the mouse block was slimmed down.

That matters more than it sounds: a release that quietly changes the format would leave a generation of slots unopenable, and the honest thing is to change the format loudly, with a version bump, when it really changes.

Get it​

The release APK is signed with the release key, so it installs over the previous version in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.13

whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.13.apk
size:   16 482 792 bytes
sha256: 98243e5577276d31f89adc1ac776bfc4242fdc0ff43f877bc36797c138cffa94

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository, and it is a single reference document rather than a folder of notes. Please read that rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

A save state that lies about its own age is a small lie, and small lies are how a tool stops being trusted. If the slot under the "Resume" button has been saying "just now" all week — this is the release you want.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 使用指南：五分钟把 DOS 游戏装进手机
item.content:encoded:
一份我想要却找不到的指南​

在自己的手机上试用这个应用时，我注意到一件事：我读过的每一份 DOSBox 指南，作者都默认你已经知道 .zip 包是什么。他们直接从有意思的部分讲起——声音芯片、存档格式、JIT——然后假定你从 1994 年起就一直在用 DOS。

对大多数拿着手机的人来说，这个假定是错的。把老游戏搬上现代手机，难的从来不是模拟器，而是最初那五分钟：怎么把游戏弄进手机，而且是应用能启动的形状。

所以我干脆写了一份我想要的那一份。七个步骤，每一步都配一张真机截图，不假设你见过命令行。

五分钟版本​

  1. 安装应用（APK 在发布页）。
  2. 打开它，落到 Files 面板，里面是空的。
  3. 按 + Install a bundle (.zip)，选一个 .zip 游戏文件。
  4. 按 Play，游戏就开始了。
  5. 随时按左上角的 File 回到列表。

就这么多。下面全是这五步背后的细节——想弄明白在做什么就读，想直接玩就跳过。

开始之前​

手机Android 5.0 及以上，手机平板都行
空间应用大约 60 MB，再加上游戏本身的大小
网络应用和游戏都在手机上之后，不需要网络
账号不需要

你还需要一个游戏，单个 .zip 文件。这里说的「游戏」不是把你自己的文件打个 ZIP——往下看游戏从哪来？。

第 1 步 —— 安装应用​

应用不在源码仓库里。它由发布流水线构建，发布在发布页上，文件名是 whereq-dosbox-<version>.apk，旁边还有一个 .sha256 文件写着校验和。

把 .apk 拷到手机上——数据线、云盘、文件传输，随你——然后在手机上点它。Android 会问要不要允许这个应用安装，允许就行。

应用会出现在你的主屏幕上，就是那个 >_ 标记：

主屏幕上的 WhereQ-DOSBox 图标。

应用列表里的名字、通知里的名字、Android 展示应用信息时写的名字，都写着 WhereQ-DOSBox：

WhereQ-DOSBox 的 Android 应用信息页。

第 2 步 —— 安装游戏​

打开应用。你会落到 Files 面板——列出已安装内容的那个界面：

全新安装后空白的 Files 面板。

两种把游戏放进去的办法，都在面板顶部：

按钮作用
+ Install a bundle (.zip)从手机里选一个 .zip
Install all bundles from a folder把某一个文件夹里的所有 .zip 一次解开

按 + Install a bundle (.zip)，系统的文件选择器会打开。选你的游戏 .zip——通常在 Downloads 里——应用会解开它并登记好。面板上就列出它了：

Files 面板里有两个已安装的游戏。

列表里每个游戏有四个按钮：

按钮作用
Play从头开始运行游戏
States为这个游戏存档、读档
Launch…换一段程序来跑，或者在游戏前加载驱动文件
Remove从应用里卸载这个游戏

游戏从哪来？​

这里的游戏是一个形状固定的 .zip：

  the bundle
  ─────────
  PLAY.BAT          the entry point - the app runs this
  <the game files>  whatever the game needs
  __meta.json       the name the app shows in the list

就这些。仓库里附送了一个，你可以照着看形状、马上试起来：examples/game-bundle——就是 STARFALL 演示版。把那个文件夹里的 whereq-demo-bundle.zip 拷到手机上装上就行。

至于真正的游戏：还在托管这些废弃 DOS 游戏的站点，一般都直接给 .zip。如果某个游戏的压缩包里只有游戏文件、没有 PLAY.BAT，应用是起不来的——自己写一个 PLAY.BAT 去运行游戏的可执行文件，再把文件夹压一次。

第 3 步 —— 开始玩​

按 Play。

模拟器会重启应用并引导游戏启动，你落到 DOS 提示符：

DOSBox 欢迎画面和 C:\> 提示符，下方是屏幕键盘。

输入游戏的名字，按 Enter。从这一刻起就是真正的游戏了——真正的键盘，真正的声音，真正的鼠标。

这是一款 1994 年的 DOS 游戏跑在手机上的样子：

Formula 1（Domark，1994）跑在手机上，四周是屏幕键盘。

这是 STARFALL 演示版：

STARFALL 的标题画面。

STARFALL 正在游戏中，画面两侧是两块键盘区。

第一次运行游戏时，Android 可能会问要不要允许这个应用发通知。它用通知来提醒你「游戏还在后台」。答哪边都行——拒绝只是少一条提醒：

Android 的通知权限对话框。

游戏在跑的时候，按左上角的 File 会把 Files 面板拉到上层，面板上会给正在跑的那个游戏显示一行 Resume：

游戏运行中拉出的 Files 面板，列表上方有 Resume F1。

第 4 步 —— 键盘和鼠标​

不用外接实体键盘，因为屏幕键盘就是键盘。横屏时画面两侧会出现两块键盘区，像掌机那样摆：左边是方向键组成的十字键加半边 QWERTY，右边是动作键（Alt、Ctrl、Shift、Space、Enter）和另外半边字母。

两个键可以切换键盘区显示的内容：

键显示
#+=标点层
FnF1–F12、Ins/Del、Home/End、PgUp/PgDn、Caps、PrtSc、Pause

切换之后，那个键会亮着。

修饰键有两种用法。 点一下 Ctrl、Alt 或 Shift，它会保持按下状态等你按下一个键——先 Ctrl 再 C。按住它，它的表现就和一个真正的键一样：手指按着多久它就保持多久，游戏里那些开火键、侧移键正是这么用的，另一只拇指同时操控方向。

鼠标就是屏幕本身。 你的手指就是鼠标：拖动是移动指针，点一下是点击，屏幕上的 RMB 键（左边那块，紧挨 Tab）是鼠标右键——在大多数 DOS 游戏里那代表取消或返回。在画面上按住第二根手指也是同一个意思，而且是在那根手指自己的位置上。

把手机转成竖屏，两块键盘区会折成底部的一条，适合画面高比宽大的游戏。

第 5 步 —— 存档​

存档是把整台机器冻住：CPU、内存、显存、声卡芯片、打开着的 DOS 文件句柄，全都冻住。读档之后，游戏正好停在你离开时的样子——哪怕中间应用被关掉过。

按 File，再按游戏旁边的 States：

Save states 面板，三个空档位。

一共有三个档位。按 Save 把当前游戏冻进档位 1，面板会告诉你是什么时候存的：

已存的档位——档位 1，两分钟前。

关掉面板，Files 面板会为这个游戏保留一行 Resume，写明是哪个档位、什么时候存的：

Resume starfall-v2 · slot 1 · just now。

Load 把游戏放回去。档位能撑过退出应用，也能撑过手机重启。

第 6 步 —— 让存档更安全​

存档默认放在应用自己的私有存储里。卸载应用时 Android 会把它删掉——手机丢了、换手机了，也一样。你的游戏和你的存档跟着一起没。

所以应用会问你一次：要不要在你自己掌管的地方再留一份：

首次存档后出现的 Keep your saves safe 提示。

应用自己的对话框里也是同一套说法，随时可以打开看：

Saves folder 对话框，尚未设置任何文件夹。

按 Choose folder，系统会问要不要允许这个应用访问手机上的某个文件夹：

系统对文件夹的授权对话框。

选好文件夹，按 USE THIS FOLDER，再按 ALLOW。从这以后每个档位都会压缩一份镜像到那个文件夹里，就放在游戏旁边。

你随时可以在 Config → Saves folder 下查看或更换这个文件夹：

设置对话框。

Saves folder 对话框，已经设置好文件夹。

两点提醒：

  • Android 不允许应用直接占用整个 Download 文件夹，那个权限太宽了。挑别的文件夹就行——Documents 完全可以。
  • 你只需要回答这一次，应用不会再问。

第 7 步 —— 重装之后，或者换了新手机​

这就是那个文件夹的用处。

把应用卸载，重新装上，选同一个文件夹。应用会进去一看，你的游戏还在——它们从来就不在应用里面：

应用卸载之后，手机上那个文件夹里的内容。

应用会认出那些没被安装的游戏，问你要不要把它们带回来：

Restore games 提示。

按 Restore，它们连名字带存档一起回来：

恢复出来的两个游戏，存档也在。

而存档仍然记得自己是什么时候存的：

恢复出来的档位，仍然写着三分钟前。

最后这一行就是整个功能的意义所在。三分钟前存的存档，就写着三分钟前——哪怕它是从文件夹里重新装回一个新装的版本。

东西都放在哪里​

  inside the app                    the folder you picked
  ────────────                      ───────────────────
  the games                         <your folder>/
  the save-state slots                <game name>/
                                       slot1.gz
                                       slot2.gz
                                       bundle.zip

  gone when the app is removed     stays until you delete it

出问题了怎么办​

你看到的意味着怎么办
「That save file is damaged」这个档位是旧版本写的存档格式升过版本号，太旧的档位会被拒绝而不是读错。重新存一个新档位。
游戏起不来包里没有 PLAY.BAT，或者入口指错了打开那个 .zip，确认 PLAY.BAT 能运行游戏的可执行文件
按 Play 没动静模拟器正在重启来引导游戏等几秒——进程是故意重启的，游戏会在新进程里起来
键盘挡住了画面两块键盘区占了画面两侧把手机转成竖屏，键盘会折成底部一条
鼠标点不动游戏要的是「按住」状态拖动用来移动；右键用屏幕上的 RMB 键，或者在画面上按住第二根手指
Download 文件夹选不了Android 不允许应用占用整个 Download换一个文件夹，比如 Documents
弹出通知授权应用想发「回到游戏」的通知允许或拒绝都行——拒绝只是少这条通知
游戏很卡模拟器跑的是当年的硬件，不是快机器这是 1994 年那台机器本来的速度，不是手机慢

接下来​

这篇就是指南。仓库里存着同一份文档，以及它背后的一切：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox——源码、示例包、问题追踪，指南本身在 docs/USER-GUIDE.md。

**技术参考**是长文——原生构建怎么做、存档机制怎么把整台机器拍下来、FM 芯片怎么被精确还原、包怎么变成一个跑起来的 DOS 程序、屏幕键盘怎么把按键送进模拟器、以及构建流水线。它是写给工程师看的，不是给拿着手机的人看的。

**发布页**上有 APK 和它的校验和。

致谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

上面每一张截图都是真机，跑的是正式签名的 APK。这里没有任何一张是效果图。

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox user guide: put a DOS game on your phone in five minutes
item.content:encoded:
The guide I wanted and could not find​

Here is a thing I noticed while I was testing the app on my own phone. Every DOSBox guide I have ever read was written by somebody who already knew what a .zip bundle was. They start at the interesting part — the sound chips, the save-state format, the JIT — and assume you have been running DOS since 1994.

That assumption is wrong for most people holding a phone. The hardest part of putting an old game on a modern phone is not the emulator. It is the first five minutes: getting the game onto the phone at all, in a shape the app can start.

So I wrote the guide I wanted instead. Seven steps, one screenshot of every screen, and no assumption that you have ever seen a command prompt.

The five-minute version​

  1. Install the app. The APK is on the releases page.
  2. Open it. You land on the Files panel, and it is empty.
  3. Press + Install a bundle (.zip) and pick a .zip game file.
  4. Press Play. The game starts.
  5. Press File (top left) whenever you want to come back to the list.

That is the whole thing. Everything below is the detail behind those five steps — read it if you want to understand what you are doing, skip it if you just want to play.

Before you start​

PhoneAndroid 5.0 or newer, any phone or tablet
Spaceabout 60 MB for the app, plus the size of the game
Networknone needed once the app and the game are on the phone
Accountnone

You also need a game, as a single .zip file. A game for this app is not the same thing as a ZIP of your own files — see Where do I get a game? below.

Step 1 — Install the app​

The app is not in the source repository. It is built by the release pipeline and published on the releases page as whereq-dosbox-<version>.apk, with a .sha256 file next to it carrying the checksum.

Copy the .apk to your phone — cable, cloud drive, a file-sharing app, whatever is at hand — then tap it on the phone. Android asks whether to allow installing from that app; allow it, and the install goes through.

The app appears on your home screen as the >_ mark:

The WhereQ-DOSBox icon on the home screen.

The name in the app list, the notification, and the screen Android shows for the app all read WhereQ-DOSBox:

The Android App info page for WhereQ-DOSBox.

Step 2 — Install a game​

Open the app. You land in the Files panel — the screen that lists what you have installed:

The Files panel on a fresh install, with no games yet.

Two ways to get a game in, both at the top of the panel:

buttonwhat it does
+ Install a bundle (.zip)pick one .zip from your phone
Install all bundles from a folderunpack every .zip in one folder at once

Press + Install a bundle (.zip), and the system's file picker opens. Pick your game's .zip — usually in Downloads — and the app unpacks it and registers it. The panel then lists it:

The Files panel with two games installed.

Each game in the list has four buttons:

buttonwhat it does
Playstart the game from the beginning
Statessave and load save states for this game
Launch…run a different program, or add driver files, before the game
Removeuninstall this game from the app

Where do I get a game?​

A game for this app is a .zip with a small, fixed shape:

  the bundle
  ─────────
  PLAY.BAT          the entry point - the app runs this
  <the game files>  whatever the game needs
  __meta.json       the name the app shows in the list

That is it. The repository ships one, so you can see the shape and try the app immediately: examples/game-bundle — the STARFALL demo. Copy whereq-demo-bundle.zip from that folder to your phone and install it.

For real games: sites that still host abandonware DOS games generally offer them as a .zip. If a game's archive contains the game files but no PLAY.BAT, the app cannot start it — make a PLAY.BAT that runs the game's executable, and zip the folder again.

Step 3 — Play the game​

Press Play.

The emulator restarts the app and boots the game, and you land at a DOS prompt:

The DOSBox welcome banner and the C:\> prompt, with the on-screen keyboard below it.

Type the game's name and press Enter. From then on it is the real game — the real keyboard, the real sound, the real mouse.

Here is a real 1994 DOS game running on a phone:

Formula 1 (Domark, 1994) running on the phone, with the on-screen keyboard around it.

And here is the STARFALL demo:

The STARFALL title screen.

STARFALL being played, with the two keyboard pads beside the picture.

The first time a game runs, Android may ask whether the app may send you notifications. It uses them for a "back to the game" reminder when you leave the app. Answer either way — declining only means you lose that reminder:

The Android notification permission prompt.

When a game is running, the File key (top left) brings the Files panel back over it, and the panel shows a Resume line for the game that is running right now:

The Files panel over a running game, with Resume F1 above the list.

Step 4 — The keyboard and the mouse​

There is no physical keyboard in the way, because the screen keyboard is the keyboard. In landscape you get two pads beside the picture, the way a handheld console is built: the left pad has the arrow keys as a D-pad and the left half of a split QWERTY, the right pad has the action keys (Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Space, Enter) and the right half of the alphabet.

Two keys change what the pads show:

keyshows
#+=the punctuation layer
FnF1–F12, Ins/Del, Home/End, PgUp/PgDn, Caps, PrtSc, Pause

The switched key lights up while its layer is on.

Modifiers work two ways. Tap Ctrl, Alt or Shift and it stays armed for the next key — Ctrl, then C. Hold it and it behaves like a real key for as long as your finger is down, which is what a game expects of its fire and strafe keys while the other thumb steers.

The mouse is the screen. Your finger is the mouse: drag to move the pointer, tap to click, and the on-screen RMB key (on the left pad, next to Tab) is the right mouse button — in most DOS games that is cancel or back. A second finger on the picture does the same, at that finger's own position.

Turn the phone to portrait and the pads fold into a single strip along the bottom, for the games that are taller than they are wide.

Step 5 — Save a state​

A save state is the whole machine frozen: the CPU, the memory, the video memory, the sound chips, the open DOS file handles. Load it and the game is exactly where you left it — even if the app was closed in between.

Press File, then States next to the game:

The Save states sheet, with three empty slots.

There are three slots. Press Save to freeze the game into slot 1, and the sheet shows when you did it:

The sheet with a saved slot — Slot 1, two minutes ago.

Close the sheet and the Files panel carries a Resume line for the game, naming the slot and the moment it was made:

The Files panel with Resume starfall-v2 · slot 1 · just now.

Load puts the game back. A slot survives quitting the app and rebooting the phone.

Step 6 — Keep your saves safe​

A save state normally lives inside the app's own private storage. Android deletes that when you uninstall the app — and when you lose the phone, or switch phones. Your games and your saves go with it.

So the app asks, once, whether you want a second copy somewhere that is yours:

The Keep your saves safe prompt, after the first save.

The app says the same thing in its own dialog, which you can open at any time:

The Saves folder dialog, with no folder set yet.

Press Choose folder, and the system asks you to allow the app into a folder on your phone:

The system permission dialog for the folder.

Pick a folder, press USE THIS FOLDER, and press ALLOW. From then on every slot is mirrored into that folder, compressed, next to the game itself.

You can see, and change, the folder at any time under Config → Saves folder:

The Settings dialog.

The Saves folder dialog, with a folder set.

Two notes:

  • Android refuses to let an app take the Download folder itself, because that would be too broad a permission. Pick any other folder — Documents is fine.
  • You only have to answer this once. The app does not ask again.

Step 7 — After a reinstall, or on a new phone​

This is what the folder is for.

Uninstall the app, install it again, and choose the same folder. The app looks inside it and finds your games — they are still there, because they were never inside the app:

The folder on the phone after the app was uninstalled.

The app notices the games that are not installed and offers to bring them back:

The Restore games prompt.

Press Restore, and they come back with their names and their saves:

Restored two games, with their saves ready.

And the save state still knows when it was made:

The restored slot, still saying three minutes ago.

That last line is the point of the whole feature. A save that was made three minutes ago says three minutes ago, even after it was rebuilt from the folder on a fresh install.

Where everything lives​

  inside the app                    the folder you picked
  ────────────                      ───────────────────
  the games                         <your folder>/
  the save-state slots                <game name>/
                                       slot1.gz
                                       slot2.gz
                                       bundle.zip

  gone when the app is removed     stays until you delete it

If something goes wrong​

what you seewhat it meanswhat to do
"That save file is damaged"the slot was written by an older versionthe save format grew a version; older slots are refused rather than misread. Start a new slot.
The game does not startthe bundle has no PLAY.BAT, or the entry point is wrongopen the .zip and check that PLAY.BAT runs the game's executable
Nothing happens when you tap Playthe emulator is restarting to boot the gamewait a few seconds — the process restarts on purpose, and the game starts in the new process
The keyboard is in the waythe pads take the sides of the screenturn the phone to portrait for a single strip along the bottom
The mouse does not clickthe game wants the mouse helddrag for movement; the on-screen RMB key, or a second finger on the picture, is the right button
You cannot pick the Download folderAndroid will not grant an app the whole Download folderpick another folder, such as Documents
You get a notification promptthe app wants to show the "back to the game" notificationallow it or decline it — you can decline, you just lose that notification
The game is slowthe emulator runs the original hardware, not a fast oneit is what the 1994 machine did. It is not the phone being slow.

Where to go next​

This post is the guide. The repository holds the same document, plus everything behind it:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — the source, the example bundle, the issues, and the guide itself at docs/USER-GUIDE.md.

The technical reference is the long one — how the native build works, how the save-state machine takes a snapshot of the whole machine, the exact FM snapshot, the bundle launcher, the on-screen keyboard, the build pipeline. It is written for engineers, not for phone holders.

The releases page carries the APK and its checksum.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

Every screenshot above is a real phone, running the release-signed APK. Nothing here is a mock-up.

item.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.10：声音也活过了存档
item.content:encoded:
那段留在后面的音乐​

你在 boss 打到一半的时候按了存档。音乐正响，那只大家伙正在做一件让人难受的事，你把手机放下，去回一条消息。

两分钟后你回来，读档。

战斗和你离开时一模一样——怪物、血条、它的坐标，样样都对。可音乐完全不在同一条时间线上：它从来没有跟机器一起被冻住，于是一切都倒回去了，它还在往前放。而 PC 喇叭那头的哔哔声还在后台嗡嗡地响，谁也不理。

那是 1.0.0.9。存档做得很好，好到只差一样东西：声音。

存档存的是一台机器，不是一块屏幕​

存档本来应该存下整台机器：CPU、内存、显存、打开的 DOS 文件句柄、硬件定时器。少了机器的任何一个部件，读回来就只是一台略有不同的机器——而这一次，你听得出来。

FM 芯片根本不在快照里。不是存得不准、不是存得不全——是压根没有。

这比听上去更糟，因为游戏冻住的时候芯片并不会跟着停。游戏运行中读档，模拟器会把它知道的一切倒回去：怪物、血条、那只大家伙的坐标、DOS 文件句柄、定时器。芯片不在它知道的那一串里，于是它继续放下去。你眼前是一场被倒带的战斗，耳朵里却是没有倒带的音乐。

如果这份存档是被恢复进一个全新的进程里——也就是关掉应用之后再按继续时发生的事——那芯片是崭新的、空白、哑的，音乐直接就没了。

PC 喇叭坏得又是第三种方式。它确实在快照里，可它是个实时输出设备，它排队的延迟和定时器索引被按着当前时钟恢复，而不是被保存时的那台机器的时钟——于是混音器继续发出一个客人根本没要求过的蜂鸣。它带着嗡声回来了。

「精确」在这里是什么意思​

修法是把芯片本身整个存下来，而不是存它的摘要。OPL 的状态是一个大约五千字节的结构体：每个运算单元的包络、波形相位、LFO 计数器、反馈历史。它被写进状态文件、再读回来，于是下一个采样点从上一个采样点停下的地方接着走。

还有一种更省事的做法，值得说清楚它为什么不够用。这个移植留着芯片的 512 个寄存器——驱动把音色写进去的那些——读档时可以重放它们。这能把音色完美地重建出来。但驱动在一首曲子的开头把音色编好，之后只发「按下」和「松开」；在这中间发生的一切都活在芯片内部，没有任何一个寄存器记录得了。于是重放寄存器就等于把每一个音符都从攻击段重新触发。音回来了，却回错了：它从头开始，而不是从原来的地方接着走。

所以寄存器重放还在，作为那些无法快照自己的 OPL 模型的兜底。但它现在只是兜底，不再是主方案。

我是怎么验的​

我让自己相信这件事成立的方式，是我希望自己被说服的方式：写一个测试程序，在 FM 芯片上编出一个持续的长音，然后等一个按键。

OPL 测试包：一个持续的长音，以及一行提示——存一个档，等一等，再读回来。

这个测试包就在仓库里，你也可以自己跑。屏幕上就写着它是什么："The tone is playing. Press any key to stop it."

然后这个移植在存档时把芯片的状态打进日志，读档时再打一遍，两边必须对得上——同样的包络、同样的波形相位、同样的 LFO 计数器、同样的寄存器内容。

这是相隔两分钟真实芯片时间的存档日志和读档日志：

savestate: OPL chip saved:    ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module saved:  exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

savestate: OPL chip restored: ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module restored: exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

一模一样。音从攻击段中间接上，继续响。

有件事你得知道​

1.0.0.9 写下的存档，1.0.0.10 读不了了。

声音芯片进了快照之后，状态文件多了一个版本号，读档端现在会拒绝旧存档，而不是硬把它读错。这才是诚实的做法——一个能读、但声音读错的存档，比一个直接说「不行」的存档更糟糕。

如果你手上有 1.0.0.9 留下的存档在意，升级之前先读出来。

一个一直按着的键​

按着某个键的时候转屏，那个键会永远按在 DOSBox 里。旋转之后布局要重建，而重建出来的布局没有告诉模拟器「手指已经抬起来了」，于是那个键一直按着，DOSBox 就一直重复它。

现在，布局重建时，所有处于按下状态的键都会被释放。

还有另一半。Ctrl 同时出现在两个地方——手柄区和折叠面板上——而代码默认它上面永远只有一根手指，于是在一处松开会把另一处也取消掉。现在它会数手指。

塞得下的启动器​

Files 面板现在会量一量自己有多少空间，再据此限制游戏列表的数量。以前装到第三个游戏，按钮会被挤出面板底边——掉下去就再也捞不回来了。

这是这一版里最小的改动，也是我最恼火它没在前三个版本里就发生的一个。

桌面版又能链接了​

存档相关的代码从来没被加进 autotools 的构建里，所以那个桌面基线——也就是那个能在笔记本上几秒钟编完、用来盯着模拟器内核别走偏的构建——从 1.0.0.8 引入存档开始就链接不过了。

我为这件事蒙了整整两个版本，因为我忙着发安卓版，一直没顾上。

原因有四条，彼此独立，但其实是同一类：构建里漏了一个源文件、少了一个头文件、一个函数本来该被条件编译掉、以及同一个静态库被连着列了两次——那是一个循环依赖，换个顺序才会暴露。

现在基线又能编译链接，也能跑。

一份文档，而不是一本流水账​
